questions.stem: During an intense weightlifting session, a gym-goer feels a burning sensation in their muscles. Which process is most likely responsible?

options.text: Aerobic respiration producing excess carbon dioxide
Anaerobic respiration producing lactic acid in the muscle cells
Anaerobic respiration producing ethanol in the muscle cells
Cramp caused by excess oxygen in the muscle tissue

questions.explanation: During intense exercise, oxygen cannot be delivered fast enough, so muscle cells switch to anaerobic respiration. In animals, this produces lactic acid, which builds up and causes the burning sensation and fatigue.

questions.stem: A brewer seals yeast in a container with sugar solution and no air. After several days, the solution contains ethanol. What type of respiration has occurred?

options.text: Aerobic respiration, because glucose was broken down
Anaerobic respiration in yeast, producing ethanol and carbon dioxide
Anaerobic respiration in yeast, producing lactic acid
Fermentation using oxygen trapped in the sugar solution

questions.explanation: In the absence of oxygen, yeast carries out anaerobic respiration (fermentation), breaking down glucose into ethanol and carbon dioxide. This is different from animal anaerobic respiration, which produces lactic acid.

questions.stem: A student claims that anaerobic respiration releases the same amount of energy as aerobic respiration. Why is this incorrect?

options.text: Anaerobic respiration does not use glucose as a substrate
Anaerobic respiration only partially breaks down glucose, so less energy is released
Anaerobic respiration takes place in the mitochondria where less energy is available
Anaerobic respiration requires more glucose to produce the same amount of energy

questions.explanation: Anaerobic respiration does not fully break down glucose — the products (lactic acid or ethanol) still contain chemical energy. This means much less energy is transferred per glucose molecule compared to aerobic respiration.

questions.stem: A baker notices that bread dough rises when left in a warm place. Which process causes the dough to rise?

options.text: Yeast cells carry out aerobic respiration, producing oxygen gas
Bacteria in the dough produce hydrogen gas
Yeast cells carry out anaerobic respiration, producing carbon dioxide gas
Heat causes air trapped in the dough to expand

questions.explanation: Yeast in the dough carries out anaerobic respiration (fermentation), producing carbon dioxide gas. The CO₂ bubbles become trapped in the dough, causing it to rise. The ethanol produced evaporates during baking.

questions.stem: A scientist cultures human muscle cells in a dish and gradually reduces the oxygen supply. What change would she observe in the cells' waste products?

options.text: The cells would start producing ethanol instead of carbon dioxide
The cells would stop respiring entirely
The cells would begin producing lactic acid as oxygen becomes insufficient
The cells would increase their production of water and carbon dioxide

questions.explanation: As oxygen decreases, human muscle cells switch from aerobic to anaerobic respiration. Animal cells produce lactic acid (not ethanol) during anaerobic respiration. The cells do not stop respiring — they switch pathway to continue releasing some energy.
